chapter_theme: Beyond sectarian observance (நிராசாரம்): those who master a sect's scriptures claim to know, but the Lord dwells with the forbearing and with those who hold his feet; sect-bound people who never turn to the Lord within weep, are reborn and perish inside the sect they could not leave.
structure_note: The chapter opens (1550) and closes (1556) on the six sects and those who stay in them. Between, verses set holding the Lord's feet against grieving neglect (1551, 1552), sort kinds of knowers (1553), and urge the mind to seek the Lord within (1554, 1555).

1550.reading: Those who stand as gods gained the six sects and, reciting the shastras, say 'we have understood'; but the First Lord stands mingled among those who know forbearance.
1550.nuance: இமையங்களாய் நின்ற தேவர்கள் is obscure: இமையவர் are the unblinking gods, but இமையங்கள் may hide another word. யமை in line 3 is read as அமை (it is settled, we know); கமை is taken as Sanskrit kshama, forbearance. The contrast between scripture-learning and forbearance is the verse's point on this reading.

1551.reading: People who bear the feet of the Lord with spreading matted hair and konrai blossom are without equal on earth; those who never think how to be freed stay in the world grieving and weeping.
1551.nuance: நேர் ஒப்பர் can mean 'they are equal' (to the gods, or to one another) or 'they are incomparable'. நீங்கிய வண்ணம் is taken as the way of release from bonds; it could also mean the way the Lord stays apart.

1552.reading: If those who weep and those whose nature has gone wrong take up rare austerity and think of the Lord there, the king of the gods keeps them from suffering, grants them greatness, and there is no more birth.
1552.nuance: The verse picks up 1551's weepers and offers them a way back: even the fallen (இயல்பு கெட்டார்) are not shut out. வானவர் கோன் here is the Lord, not Indra.

1553.reading: Those of deep knowledge do not think of any helper; those of worldly knowledge eat the fruit that falls to them; those of dark knowledge are born again, mixed in the world; those who know the water become the great tall cloud.
1553.nuance: The four kinds of knower turn on puns I can't fix: தூர் (root, depth, or far), பார் (the earth), கார் (darkness, or the rain-season) and நீர் (water, or one's true nature, நீர்மை). The cloud of the last line may be one who, knowing, gives to all as rain does; that is a guess.

1554.reading: Though they see the sign of the boat, called up with knowledge, spilling its load with its mast and its old home, the people of cruel deeds do not think to cling to the red feet.
1554.nuance: The boat is commonly taken as the body that carries the soul; பறி (mast, or a fish-basket, or plunder) and பழம்பதி (the old dwelling) are unclear. The plain point stands: people see the body break up and still don't turn to the feet.

1555.reading: If I say the one who abides is the one who dwells in the mind, people scorn it, these poor fools; mind, draw near and worship, and there you can reach even the one who has no companion.
1555.nuance: மனோமயன், he who is made of or dwells in the mind, is the claim people scorn. துணையிலி, the one with no companion or equal, recalls the Kural's தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான். The verse turns from the scorners to address its own mind.

1556.reading: Though the light within Om rises within them, they do not gain the experience free of the ego; before death they do not reach freedom from birth; they stood inside the sect they never left and perished.
1556.nuance: ஓங்காரத்துள் ஒளி is a yogic term for the light seen in meditation on Om. ஆங்காரம் அற்ற அனுபவம is the experience of Siva without the 'I'. The verse's fault is not the sect as such but never moving beyond it (நீங்காச் சமயம்).

links.note: Both name the Lord as the one without equal and make reaching him the cure for the mind: the Kural's தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான் removes the mind's anxiety, Tirumular's துணையிலி is reached by the mind that draws near.
329 calls those held by the mala of deluding sects great fools; 1556 says those who never leave their sect die before reaching freedom from birth. Both treat staying in a sect as the obstacle.

Kural 2 asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge; 1550 says those who recite the shastras claim to understand, but the First Lord stands among those who know கமை, forbearance. Both deny that learning reaches the Lord; 1550, on the reading of கமை as kshama, names forbearance rather than worship as what does.

Kural 7 says the mind's anxiety is hard to remove except for those who reach the feet of the incomparable one; 1551 says those who bear the Lord's feet are without equal, while those who never think of release stay in the world grieving and weeping (ஏங்கி ... அழுவாரே). Both make the feet the only cure for a grief the Kural calls மனக்கவலை and Tirumular shows as weeping.

187 says that even seeing all that grows on the branch die, people do not praise the Lord's feet; 1554 says that even seeing the sign of the boat spilling its load, people of cruel deeds do not think to cling to the red feet. Both turn on கண்டும், 'even seeing': the sight of perishing is in plain view and still does not turn anyone to the feet.

Naladiyar 25 says one who sees kin wailing as a corpse is carried to the burning ground (கண்டும்) still marries and thinks there is joy here; 1554 says those who see the boat break up (கண்டும்) still do not cling to the feet. Both are about the sight of death failing to teach; the Naladiyar's failure is to keep seeking pleasure, Tirumular's is not to seek the Lord.

1556 says those who never left their sect (நீங்காச் சமயம்) do not gain the experience free of ego and perish there; 2838 says those who stand in clarity without knowing even a trace of the sects in themselves (சமயச் சுவடும்) become lords over the gods. 2838 states the positive end of what 1556 shows failing: release lies in leaving no trace of sect, not in choosing the right one.

source_issues: 1550: இமையங்கள் and யமை (line 3) are unclear and may be corrupt; read here as இமையவர் and அமை.
